source.title: Badllama 3: removing safety finetuning from Llama 3 in minutes

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It reports results for RO, described as removing the component along the difference-in-means refusal direction across layers and token positions, and evaluates harmful-request outcomes and general benchmarks on Llama 3 8B and 70B.
record.gate_note: The paper also describes activation addition, but reports no outcome for adding the direction. QLoRA and ReFT results are not rows because those methods do not apply the claim's direction. The helpfulness benchmark values and HarmBench category values below are reported for RO; the standard-behavior aggregate is shown only in Figure 2. The study gives no outcome for activation addition.
record.test_reason: The paper independently runs HarmBench and tinyBenchmarks on the Llama 3 8B and 70B weights from the original authors (Arditi et al.), with the difference-in-means direction ablated ('Ortho'/RO). It reports ASR and capability results against the unmodified baseline. The method matches the original. Measures are HarmBench ASR plus Open LLM Leaderboard-style accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that standard and newer fine-tuning methods (QLoRA, ReFT, Ortho) strip Llama 3's safety in minutes at low cost without compromising benchmark performance. They report ASR comparable to top HarmBench jailbreaks and project a further 2–10× cost reduction by 2025. The Ortho results come from the original authors' weights, not an in-house run.
record.recipe_differences: The paper describes the same difference-in-means refusal direction and projection out across residual activations at all layers and token positions. The benchmark evaluation uses original RO weights obtained in private correspondence; whether the authors themselves extracted the direction or performed the intervention is not stated.

fits_no_version.finding: RO copyright matching scores are unchanged on 8B (27→27) and rise slightly on 70B (33→38). The metric requires correct reproduction of copyrighted text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction ablation does not raise verbatim copyrighted-content reproduction measured by hash matching.

record.problems: The RO evaluation uses weights obtained in private correspondence, and the paper says in-house evaluation is future work. HarmBench ASR measures attempts to answer, not answer quality; the authors defer quantifying generation quality. The standard-behaviour aggregate is presented only in a figure. Helpfulness evaluation uses tinyBenchmarks, and the paper calls its current OpenLLM evaluation brittle.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. QLoRA and ReFT benchmark outcomes are not included because they do not test the single-direction intervention. The standard-behaviour Figure 2 aggregates are retained as figure-only rows r13-r14.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal: the method is described but no result is reported. Refusal rate on harmless prompts is not measured. Generation quality is not measured (ASR counts attempts only).
Community abliterated releases are not evaluated; only the original authors' privately shared weights are. The paper does not state explicitly how the edit was applied to the weights.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not the original source, but its RO evaluation uses weights the original authors supplied privately. The authors plan in-house replication as future work. The abstract's '1 minute' timing is a compute-cost claim with no row. No uncertainty is reported. V2 linking rests on the evaluated artifact being distributed weights.

versions.untested_parts: Tests removal using RO, but not addition of the direction to induce refusals. It measures harmful-request ASR rather than a direct refusal rate, and evaluates general capability only on the listed multiple-choice benchmarks.
The paper does not state that the evaluated ablation was converted into a weight edit or released as an abliteration artifact.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Does not compare a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
Does not test transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not test how refusal-training choices determine whether a removable direction exists.

relationships.reason: ASR rises from 0–40% to 80–100% in every non-copyright category (r15, r17–r22, r24–r28). Capability stays within about 3 points (r1–r5, r7–r12).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose from 0–40% to 80–100% in every non-copyright category, while five of six capability benchmarks per model stayed within about 3 points.

relation.reason: It reports its own HarmBench and tinyBenchmarks results for RO against the unmodified Llama 3 8B and 70B baselines.

tranche.reason: Same difference-in-means direction, ablated at all layers and tokens, scored on HarmBench ASR and capability benchmarks as in the original's weight-edit test. Caveat: these are the original authors' own weights, re-evaluated rather than rebuilt in-house.

source_check.notes: RO results come from Arditi et al.'s own Llama 3 weights, obtained privately; the in-house Ortho run is listed as future work. So this re-evaluates the original artifact and is not an independent rebuild. No uncertainty is given. ASR counts attempts, not answer quality. All of HarmBench (val+test) standard behaviours is used; contextual behaviours are excluded. The only control is the unmodified baseline, with no random direction.

statements.correction: Llama 3 8B RO: tinyGSM8k 75.95->71.41 (-4.54); other 8B tinyBenchmarks within 2.87 (tinyHellaswag 82.15->79.28). Llama 3 70B RO: all within 1.95 (tinyTruthfulQA 59.87->57.92). HarmBench non-copyright: baseline 0.00-40.00, RO 80.00-100.00 (Tables 4-5).
statements.problem: 'tinyBenchmarks within about 3 points' is wrong for Llama 3 8B tinyGSM8k, which fell 4.54 points. The text implies the HarmBench classifier through the HarmBench harness but never names it.

statements.correction: Llama 3 70B is outside 2B-24B. For this study: 8B tinyARC 62.58->61.62; 70B tinyTruthfulQA 59.87->57.92; largest cost 8B tinyGSM8k 75.95->71.41. Weights obtained from the original authors in private correspondence.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the conditions give '2B-24B instruct models' while listing Llama 3 70B. The study's largest RO capability cost is not mentioned here.
